raw_response:
The reported hang is consistent with sender-lifetime semantics: tonic’s `Streaming` is body/decoder-based (not itself an mpsc wrapper), and a cancelled body is only converted to stream termination when the body reports the cancellation error. Tokio’s receiver returns `None` only after all sender handles are dropped and buffered items are drained.

Relevant files:

- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L18-L36](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L18-L36) - `Streaming<T>` and `StreamingInner`; wraps the HTTP body and decoder, not an mpsc receiver.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L232-L263](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L232-L263) - `StreamingInner::poll_data`; maps a request-side `Code::Cancelled` body error to `Ok(None)`, while response-side cancellation becomes `Err(Status)`.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L289-L324](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L289-L324) - `Streaming::message`; maps `poll_next`’s `None` to `Ok(None)` and status items to errors.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L380-L406](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/decode.rs?L380-L406) - `Streaming<T>::poll_next`; decodes messages, polls the body, then polls trailers; body completion yields `None`, body errors yield `Some(Err(...))`.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/client/grpc.rs?L322-L357](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/client/grpc.rs?L322-L357) - client response path constructing `Streaming` around the transport response body.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/server/grpc.rs?L423-L463](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/server/grpc.rs?L423-L463) - server `map_response`; a stream of `Result<T, Status>` is passed to `encode_server`, including `Err(Status::cancelled(...))`.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:tonic/src/codec/encode.rs?L55-L75](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/tonic/src/codec/encode.rs?L55-L75) - server stream encoder boundary consuming `Stream<Item = Result<... , Status>>`; relevant for converting a server-side status into response-body output.
- [sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0:examples/src/cancellation/server.rs?L35-L45](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tonic--v0.11.0/-/blob/examples/src/cancellation/server.rs?L35-L45) - example server-side `Err(Status::cancelled(...))`.
- [sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0:tokio/src/sync/mpsc/bounded.rs?L466-L489](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/bounded.rs?L466-L489) - public `Receiver::poll_recv`, delegating to `Chan::recv`.
- [sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0:tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L244-L296](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L244-L296) - `Chan::recv`; returns `Some(value)` for queued values, `None` for `Read::Closed`, otherwise registers the waker and remains pending.
- [sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0:tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L64-L70](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L64-L70) - `tx_count`; channel send-side closure occurs only when the outstanding sender count reaches zero.
- [sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0:tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L200-L220](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L200-L220) - sender-handle `Drop`; the final sender drop closes the channel and wakes the receiver.
- [sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0:tokio/src/sync/mpsc/bounded.rs?L1412-L1418](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/bounded.rs?L1412-L1418) - `Sender::clone`; every clone increments the effective sender lifetime.
- [sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0:tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L232-L242](/r/github.com/sg-evals/tokio--tokio-1.36.0/-/blob/tokio/src/sync/mpsc/chan.rs?L232-L242) - receiver/channel close path; closure wakes waiting receivers, but does not imply that an unrelated sender clone has been dropped.

Cross-repo conclusion: the direct chain is `Streaming::poll_next` → transport `Body::poll_data`/`poll_trailers`, not `Streaming` → Tokio mpsc. Where an application or adapter uses `ReceiverStream`, the analogous chain is `ReceiverStream::poll_next` → `Receiver::poll_recv` → `Chan::recv`. A wire-level `RST_STREAM` or a server-emitted cancelled status does not synchronously drop every application-held sender clone. Until the final `Sender` is dropped, Tokio’s receiver remains open and `poll_recv` can stay pending; therefore a client-side `next()` cannot be expected to return `None` merely because tcpdump shows cancellation.
